sections.name: PARTIES
sentences: Plaintiff Ronald Watson, an adult Black person/resides at 1500 E. Washington Lane, Philadelphia, PA 19138.
Defendant, Generation Metal Technologies, Inc. (hereinafter "Generation 1") is a corporation with a place of business located at 7811 Second Street, Trevose, PA 19053.
Defendant, Generation Metal Stamping & Machining, Inc. (hereinafter "Generation 2") is a corporation with a place of business located at 7 Colby Lane, Langhorne, PA 19047.

sections.name: FACTUAL ALLEGATIONS
sentences: On or about April 9, 2018, plaintiff commenced Employment with defendants as a Die Setter/Press Operator.
Defendants employed plaintiff either individually and/or jointly.
Plaintiff was qualified for the position of Die Setter/Press Operator.
During his employment, plaintiff was the only African American Die Setter/Press Operator employed by defendants.
The other three similarly situated Die Setters/press Operators were White.
During the course of plaintiff's employment with defendants, defendant's agents treated him less favorably than his similarly situated White coworkers.
Plaintiff's supervisors included defendants' agents Dale Leshere (White Manager), and Michael Bloschichak (White Owner).
In about April 2019, Defendants hired Thomas Kaupp (White) as a shipping and receiving worker.
Starting in about June/July 2019, Mr. Kaupp started training to use plaintiff's drill press.
Mr. Leshere and Mr. Bloschichak would come over and ask plaintiff to step aside so Mr. Kaupp could do some work on his drill press.
On or about October 16, 2019, plaintiff was on his break at 1:55 P.M., when Mr. Bloschichak falsely accused him of talking too loudly.
Mr. Bloschichak began yelling at plaintiff in his face.
Plaintiff was not talking at all during work and he never talks to the other workers.
Additionally, Mr. Bfoschiak's office is so far away from plaintiff's press, there is no way he could have heard plaintiff speaking softly or loudly.

Mr. Bfoschichak's false accusation and the way he was getting in plaintiff's face was so upsetting to plaintiff, plaintiff was shaken, and he thereafter asked Mr. Leshere if he could leave early for the day because he was unable to concentrate.
Previous to October 16, 2019, plaintiff and his White co-workers had often left the workplace early without incident so long as they got permission from Mr. Leshere.

sections.name: COUNT I - SECTION 1981_RACIAL DISCRIMINATION
sentences: Plaintiff repeats paragraphs 1-35 as if more fully set forth herein.
By and through its conduct and the conduct of its agents, Defendants violated Section 1981 by intentionally terminating plaintiff because he is Black.
Plaintiff seeks damages caused by the loss of his job and other relief noted herein above.

sections.name: PRAYER FOR RELIEF
sentences: WHEREFORE, plaintiff demands that judgment be entered in his favor and against defendants, either individually, jointly or severally, for lost pay and other financial losses, emotional pain and suffering, punitive damages, reasonable attorneys' fees and court costs, and any other relief that this Honorable Court deems to be fair and proper.
